title: Spectacles: Machine-Checkable Proofs for NLP Benchmark Scoring

reviewers.name: Cesar Sanchez
reviewers.key_strength: Novel grounding in Schützenberger's rational power series provides principled characterization of WFA-representable metrics.
reviewers.key_weakness: The 15 Lean sorrys and unverified Lean-to-Rust gap fundamentally undermine the machine-checkable correctness claim.

reviewers.name: Roderick Bloem
reviewers.key_strength: Addresses a genuine gap in ML evaluation integrity with a practical, deployable STARK proof pipeline.
reviewers.key_weakness: Specification fidelity—whether the WFA formalization captures practitioner-intended metric semantics—is assumed rather than verified.

reviewers.name: Vasco Vasconcelos
reviewers.key_strength: Elegant typed semiring abstraction unifies diverse NLP metrics under a single algebraic compilation framework.
reviewers.key_weakness: The denotational-to-operational semantics gap between Lean specification and Rust engine is tested but not formally proven.

consensus_strengths: Novel and principled application of Schützenberger's rational power series theory to characterize WFA-representable NLP metrics
Practical STARK proof performance (270 KiB proofs, 1.5ms verification) demonstrates real-world deployability
Bug-finding during formalization validates the safety value of formal specification even before verification is complete
Honest and theoretically grounded coverage analysis (21/31 metrics) derived from algebraic properties rather than ad hoc arguments
consensus_weaknesses: The 15 remaining Lean sorrys leave the formalization incomplete and potentially unsound, undermining the machine-checkable claim
The Lean-to-Rust compilation gap is validated only by differential testing, not by verified extraction or a machine-checked adequacy theorem
STARK proofs certify circuit execution fidelity, not metric correctness—the distinction is insufficiently acknowledged
Specification fidelity to practitioner-intended metric semantics is assumed rather than systematically validated against variant ambiguity
O(n²) STARK scaling and 33% metric non-coverage limit practical applicability to short-sequence, string-matching-only evaluation scenarios
actionable_recommendations: Categorize and discharge the 15 Lean sorrys, prioritizing those on the critical path for end-to-end correctness theorems
Close the Lean-to-Rust gap via verified extraction (e.g., Lean 4 native code generation or a machine-checked bisimulation between the specification and engine)
Articulate a precise trust model that distinguishes circuit execution fidelity, WFA compilation correctness, specification correspondence, and specification intent
Address specification ambiguity by parameterizing Lean specifications over metric variant choices and validating against multiple reference implementations
Investigate recursive STARK composition and weighted pushdown automata to address scaling limitations and extend coverage beyond rational power series
